title: Payment adjustments, approval dates and school board votes
question: What changed when the underlying decisions were matched to a second source?
finding: Six cases and three school votes now identify the underlying approval, payment evidence or confirmed rate.
how: Join on the lease, grant, contract or facility identifier. Check each event against the law, contract terms and comparison year in effect.
limits: A ceiling, configured rate, recorded vote or passenger threshold needs separate evidence to establish actual cash received or paid.

rows.test: Did counting only the service start date bypass the Board’s ten-year review, and did the City rebid the contract?
rows.record: HSS counted from a July service launch. The signed agreement began in March, and its ninth amendment pushed the term past the Charter’s ten-year review threshold.
rows.limit: Obtain the HSS contract-inventory review requested by the analysts, including other agreements tested, their signed start dates and any referrals to supervisors.

source.t: Original agreement, section 2 and implementation terms

rows.test: Which approval arrived late and which claims and counterclaims were later settled in the hospital design dispute?
rows.record: Public Works missed the required vote on a $1,013,500 design amendment. Years later, a settlement of competing claims specified $7.35 million to the City and $750,000 to the architects.
rows.limit: Obtain the Treasury deposit, remittance and project ledger showing receipt and use of the $7,350,000, including any insurer or third-party payor and booking date.

source.t: 2013 Budget and Legislative Analyst report, File 121210, item 3, pp. 3-1 through 3-7 and modification schedule

rows.test: Were software finalists asked to price the same deliverables, and how much of the final ceiling was paid?
rows.record: Fifty vendors answered a request for information. A legal waiver let the City select OpenGov, but finalists never priced the same deliverables.
rows.limit: Obtain the executed first amendment, acceptance criteria for later milestones, signed acceptance records, invoices, payment dates and the latest Inspector General findings on the system’s permit controls.

source.t: City supplier contract 1000036689, registered maximum amount, term, waived solicitation

rows.test: Which youth grants first crossed the applicable approval threshold and what did supervisors eventually authorize?
rows.record: A $24.75 million youth employment agreement began without a Board vote. Reviewing it exposed two more grants that had crossed the $10 million threshold.
rows.limit: Obtain the dated DCYF grant-inventory review, Controller exception reports and completed City Attorney signoffs. Trace agreements above the applicable threshold to Board approval before execution and document any remaining exceptions.

source.t: October 27 budget analysis, File 210960, grant history and policy consideration

rows.test: How did airport construction and passenger volumes affect the bid term and the duty to resume minimum rent?
rows.record: SFO attributed a 2019 lease holdover to administrative delay. Later, boarding counts crossed the lease’s threshold for restoring minimum rent. The public records identify the threshold date and leave the actual billing open.
rows.limit: Obtain the monthly ledger, sales statements, suspension and reinstatement notices, true-ups, relief credits, final occupancy date and cleared payments for lease 09-0176.

source.t: May 2019 budget analyst report, PDF pp. 12–14

rows.test: Did historical Medicare quality scores change the configured payment rate for the City hospital’s dialysis facility?
rows.record: CMS assigned the hospital renal center a 1.5% reduction on eligible 2026 Medicare dialysis payments after it scored 29 points. The California average was 55.
rows.limit: Obtain payment-year aggregate eligible Medicare dialysis payments, final adjustments and reconsideration outcomes for CCNs 052813 and 052397.
